_doc: Which of the 34 seen target tasks need a spatial-relation judgment (decision D6). Evidence: spatial_keyword_counts.json (spatial words in every instruction variant of meta/tasks.jsonl).
rule: A task is spatial when the main instruction the policy receives (annotation.human.task_description, not the subtask annotations) picks its target or goal by a relation the policy must resolve in the scene: left / right, front / rear / center, top of several, under an object, next to / near, stacking order by relative size; or when the goal is to bring the robot to a named place (navigation). Not spatial: target named only by object category or by a single container, or a word like 'on top' that only names the normal closed position.

spatial.CoffeeSetupMug: place the mug under the coffee machine dispenser
spatial.NavigateKitchen: navigate to a named fixture or object (robot-to-object relation)
spatial.TurnOffStove: turn off the front / rear, left / center / right burner
spatial.DeliverStraw: take a straw from the drawer in front
spatial.PrepareCoffee: place the mug under the coffee machine dispenser
spatial.SearingMeat: place the pan on the rear / front, left / center / right burner
spatial.StackBowlsCabinet: place the smaller bowl on top of the larger one

borderline_not_in_group.KettleBoiling: main instruction 'place the kettle on a stove burner, then turn the burner on' has no relation word, but the burner to turn on is the one under the kettle; left / front words appear only in subtask annotations
borderline_not_in_group.PackIdenticalLunches: 'each tupperware on the nearby counter': 'nearby' may or may not disambiguate the counter
borderline_not_in_group.SetUpCuttingStation: 'left drawer' appears only in subtask annotations, not in the main instruction
